newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Russia, Ukraine ready for Yeltsin visit, spokesman.
newsitem.headline: Russia, Ukraine ready for Yeltsin visit, spokesman.

text.p: Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma and Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin ironed out differences between the two states on Wednesday, paving the way for a long-postponed visit by President Boris Yeltsin to Kiev, Kuchma's aide said.

"After three hours of talks the sides came to decisions which removed all problems standing in the way of the forthcoming visit of the Russian president," spokesman Dmytro Markov told reporters after tough talks dominated by a row over the disputed Black Sea Fleet and trade issues.

Yeltsin is expected to visit Ukraine on Friday and Saturday to sign a long-delayed friendship treaty between the two Slav pillars of the Commonwealth of Independent States which groups 12 former Soviet republics. He has not made an official bilateral visit to Kiev since the breakup of the Soviet Union in 1991.
"The sides have voiced concern over dramatic decline in the trade turnover and decided to lift all bariers which stand on the way of the bilateral trade," Markov said.

He did not mention another painful problem discussed by Chernomyrdin and Kuchma -- the final shareout of the disputed Black Sea Fleet and the fate of its main base of Sevastopol. Chernomyrdin has said solving this issue was crucial to allow Yeltsin's visit to go ahead.

Markov said Ukrainian Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko and Chernomyrdin will sign bilateral documents later on Wednesday but did not specify which. A deal on the fleet has been expected to be one of the accords. Chernomyrdin was expected to leave Kiev late on Wednesday.
